papers.title: Behavioral arousal organizes visual cortical population micro-states across the sleep-wake cycle
papers.summary: Using two-photon calcium imaging of mouse V1 layer II/III pyramidal neurons, the study found that cortical population activity organizes into recurring micro-states that span conventional sleep-wake boundaries. A Hidden Markov Model revealed that micro-state organization was more strongly aligned with behavioral arousal (pupil diameter, orofacial motion) than with discrete NREM-wake categories, with two functionally opposing ensembles tracking the arousal axis in opposite directions.

papers.title: Beyond circadian: a yearlong prospective cohort study into human sleep using subcutaneously implanted electroencephalography
papers.summary: A yearlong prospective cohort study used subcutaneously implanted EEG in 20 healthy adults to track ultralong-term sleep architecture under real-world conditions. Key findings included seasonal effects (early summer shorter total sleep time and REM duration), weather effects (sunshine shorter sleep latency; cloud cover longer latency; higher temperature earlier sleep timing and reduced deep sleep), weekend delays in sleep timing, social jetlag in a minority, and no robust multi-day intrinsic cycles.

papers.title: Probing the Glymphatic System Using Optical Imaging and Mathematical Modeling
papers.summary: This study combined optical imaging in rats with mathematical modeling (advection-diffusion PDE) to probe glymphatic tracer transport under different isoflurane anesthesia levels (1.5%, 2%, 3%) and tracer molecular weights (1 kDa, 160 kDa). Optimal parameters showed tight clustering of diffusion coefficients but wider spread of CSF flow velocities.

papers.title: SPDAlign: Interpretable Riemannian Alignment for EEG Forward Modeling Shifts
papers.summary: The paper introduces SPDAlign, an interpretable Riemannian alignment framework for EEG domain adaptation that theoretically recovers forward-model distribution shifts via linear transformations on the SPD manifold and aligns domain means and rotations using Wasserstein Procrustes. Simulations and public EEG datasets show competitive performance.

papers.title: The sleep EEG spectral profile of narcolepsy with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea more closely resembles narcolepsy than obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: This retrospective spectral analysis compared sleep EEG in 224 treatment-naïve adults with narcolepsy with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea (NT-OSA), narcolepsy alone (NT), and OSA alone, plus 39 sleepy controls. NT-OSA showed spectral profiles more similar to NT than OSA across polysomnography and MSLT, with effect-size profile correlations of 0.76–0.78 (both P < 0.001).

papers.title: Detecting EEG index of arousal in sleeping patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome.
papers.summary: Nighttime polysomnography in patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, minimally conscious state patients, and healthy controls showed that EEG spectral slope indexed arousal across sleep stages in all groups, while spectral entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity indexed awareness, differing significantly between conscious and unconscious states.

papers.title: Coordinated Brain-Heart Dynamics During Human NREM Sleep
papers.summary: Developed a Joint Phase-Amplitude Coupling (JPAC) metric to quantify coordination between cortical slow oscillations, sleep spindles, and cardiac timing during NREM sleep in 30 healthy adults. Stronger JPAC was associated with higher high-frequency heart rate variability, steeper spectral slopes, and lower neural complexity, indicating enhanced neurovisceral integration during synchronized, parasympathetically dominated NREM sleep.

papers.title: Frontal aperiodic activity and sensorimotor theta clustering are differentially modulated by tDCS during proprioceptive training in Parkinson's disease: An EEG study.
papers.summary: Investigated whether six sessions of anodal tDCS over the supplementary motor area combined with proprioceptive training modulate EEG aperiodic activity, Lempel-Ziv complexity (LZC), and theta clustering in 24 individuals with Parkinson's disease. Significant group×time interactions showed that sham tDCS led to flattening of the aperiodic exponent, reduced offset, and increased LZC and theta clustering, while active tDCS remained stable or decreased, suggesting tDCS may accelerate the transition to automatic sensorimotor processing.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture pretreatment ameliorates sleep deprivation-induced cardiac dysfunction via the regulation of GABAergic neuron activity in the cerebellar fastigial nucleus.
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of sleep deprivation, this study demonstrated that electroacupuncture (EA) pretreatment restores the activity of GABAergic neurons in the cerebellar fastigial nucleus and ameliorates cardiac dysfunction. Chemogenetic inhibition of these neurons abolished the cardioprotective effects of EA, indicating that EA protects against sleep deprivation-induced cardiac injury by modulating FNGABA neuronal activity.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Sleep Heart Rate Estimation from Accelerometers: Toward Population-Scale Cardiac Insight Without Optical Sensors
papers.summary: Presented SeqSmoother, a transformer-based temporal corrector for estimating sleep heart rate from wrist accelerometry without optical sensors, using spectral descriptors and a physics-motivated sub-harmonic feature. Across 13 participant-disjoint folds, SeqSmoother achieved a participant-macro MAE of 1.60 bpm and provided estimates over a larger portion of eligible recordings than the Nightbeat implementation, with the sub-harmonic ratio achieving an AUROC of 0.972 for harmonic lock-on detection.

papers.title: A microglial circadian clock sculpts synapses during neurodevelopment.
papers.summary: Commentary on a recent study by Routh and colleagues showing that the microglial circadian clock regulates synaptic refinement during a critical period of neurodevelopment in mice. Loss of Bmal1 in microglia induced a proinflammatory state and excessive pruning of synapses, primarily in adolescent male mice, revealing a sex-dependent role for the microglial clock in sculpting synapses.

papers.title: REV-ERBs as regulators of circadian rhythm, neuroinflammation, and glial lipid homeostasis in Alzheimer's disease. A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that REV-ERBα/β nuclear receptors integrate circadian, metabolic, and neuroimmune pathways in Alzheimer's disease, with preclinical data showing pan-REV-ERB agonists reduce glial activation, restore NCoR/HDAC3 repression, improve cognition, and partially realign circadian rhythms, though compounds have pharmacokinetic and off-target limitations.

papers.title: EEG Signatures Support a Shrinking Spotlight of Attention After Errors.
papers.summary: Using EEG in 21 participants during a luminance-varying flanker task, the study found that frontal midline theta power related to increased decision threshold and faster drift rate, but these relationships were not modulated by errors. After errors, the relationship between posterior alpha/beta power and drift rate was enhanced, supporting separate roles for midfrontal control and sensory-specific attentional adjustment.

papers.title: Post-weaning threonine supplementation improves social memory in female offspring exposed to maternal sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of late-gestational maternal sleep deprivation, adult female offspring showed selectively impaired social memory and reduced serum L-threonine; post-weaning threonine supplementation improved social memory and colonic mucus thickness, attenuated hippocampal neuroinflammation, and restored synaptic plasticity proteins, with the mucus benefit blocked by DSS co-treatment.

papers.title: Mental health risk stratification using heart rate variability and prefrontal electroencephalography: eXtreme gradient boosting-based classifier and latent class analysis-based subtyping.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous HRV and prefrontal EEG, this study built a mixed graphical model, XGBoost classifier, and latent profile analysis to stratify mental health risk; the classifier distinguished healthy controls from psychiatric patients with 74.9% accuracy using anxiety, middle-beta power, and low-frequency HRV, and identified three patient subtypes including hyperarousal, relatively stable, and frontal EEG slowing.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG and EEG-Derived Markers of Severity, Prognosis, and Recovery After Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 33 studies (1,696 stroke or suspected-stroke participants) found that greater EEG/QEEG abnormality—especially increased slow-wave activity and higher delta/alpha or delta-theta/alpha-beta ratios—was consistently associated with greater severity, larger lesion burden, and poorer functional outcomes, but evidence was heterogeneous with low to very-low certainty and no universal prognostic threshold could be supported.

papers.title: Aerospace stressors and brain health in military aviators: a glymphatic-neurovascular framework.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a glymphatic-neurovascular framework in which military aviation stressors (hypobaria, intermittent hypoxia/hyperoxia, high +Gz, sleep/circadian disruption, wakefulness-promoting agents, noise, radiation, chemicals) may converge on neurovascular, blood-brain barrier, perivascular, and inflammatory pathways, while noting that direct human evidence of glymphatic dysfunction in aviators is absent and calling for exposure-resolved longitudinal research.

papers.title: Nighttime Respiratory Disturbance and Hypoxemia Associated with Impaired Linear Growth in Children with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cross-sectional study of 2,443 children with suspected obstructive sleep apnea, higher nocturnal hypoxemia (T90%) but not apnea-hypopnea index was independently associated with lower height z-scores, and moderate-to-severe OSA and the highest T90% quartile were associated with increased odds of subclinical growth impairment.

papers.title: Tanshinone IIA Ameliorates Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment: Involvement of Gut Microbiota and the TLR4/NF-κB Signaling Pathway.
papers.journal: The American journal of Chinese medicine
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived rats, tanshinone IIA improved cognitive function, reduced hippocampal inflammation and neuronal death, and attenuated blood-brain barrier disruption, effects associated with gut microbiota regulation, reduced LPS leakage, and modulation of TLR4/NF-κB signaling.

papers.title: Micro-recovery dosing in elite sport: an initiative-taking, organization-wide recovery framework.
papers.summary: Proposes a structural framework for micro-recovery dosing (MRD), involving proactively planned 36-hour multidimensional recovery periods at five to eight instances per year embedded in the competitive season, extending to all high-performance organization members. It argues for shifting from incidental recovery gaps to an intentionally designed recovery architecture and identifies the active ingredient problem as the central scientific challenge.

papers.title: Maternal circadian rhythm writes immune fate in offspring.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a recent Caenorhabditis elegans study showing that maternal circadian entrainment rhythmically alters offspring basal irg-5 expression and infection vulnerability, proposing mechanistic and evolutionary bet-hedging interpretations.

papers.title: Electroencephalography (EEG) and Quantitative EEG for Acute Stroke Triage and Post-Reperfusion Monitoring: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 15 studies found that EEG and quantitative EEG show candidate value for acute stroke triage and post-reperfusion monitoring, but evidence heterogeneity prevented pooled diagnostic accuracy estimates and certainty was very low to low.

papers.title: ANGPTL2 and CP define complementary circadian-associated signals in atrial fibrillation: integrative transcriptomics and external validation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Integrative transcriptomics and external validation identified ANGPTL2 and CP as circadian-associated genes consistently upregulated in fibrillating atria, with distinct expression profiles and enrichment in vascular and stromal cell populations, but no compound met criteria for cross-cohort drug repurposing.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in drug-resistant epilepsy: A randomized, sham-controlled crossover trial with exploratory EEG and MRI response phenotyping.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled crossover pilot trial with 14 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients, active taVNS did not significantly outperform sham stimulation for seizure reduction (mean SRR 46.26% active vs 48.62% sham). Greater EEG beta-band attenuation in occipital and frontal regions was associated with larger active-specific benefit, while bilateral structural abnormalities and limbic involvement were more frequent among nonresponders.

papers.title: Diagnosing Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in adulthood: A scoping review of diagnostic challenges and age-related electroclinical evolution.
papers.summary: A scoping review of 45 sources encompassing 421 patients found that classical Lennox-Gastaut syndrome features are attenuated or under-documented in adulthood, with fulfillment of ILAE seizure-type criteria decreasing from 73% in childhood to 41% in adulthood and mandatory EEG hallmarks documented in less than half of adult patients. The authors recommend a longitudinal diagnostic mindset and age-adapted frameworks to avoid underdiagnosis.

papers.title: Environmental circadian disruption alters rhythmicity of clock and epigenetic gene expression in SKH-1 female mouse livers.
papers.summary: The study measured relative gene expression in female SKH-1 mouse livers under normal and disrupted light schedules to test whether environmental circadian disruption alters rhythmic expression of core clock and epigenetic regulatory genes. Disruption caused significant loss of rhythmic expression in 5 of 8 core clock genes (Cry1, Cry2, Npas2, Nr1d1, Per2), loss of rhythmicity in all active demethylases and Zfp57, and slight damping of Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b rhythmicity.

papers.title: Smartphone addiction and self-esteem among university students: a moderated mediation and latent profile analysis.
papers.summary: Examined associations between smartphone addiction and self-esteem in 1,130 university students, testing sleep quality and physical learning engagement as mediators and gender as moderator using moderated serial mediation and latent profile analysis. Found smartphone addiction positively associated with sleep quality and self-esteem, with sleep quality mediating the association for both genders, and identified three distinct subgroups based on sleep quality and physical learning engagement that differed in smartphone addiction and self-esteem.

papers.title: Photoperiod-entrained circadian regulation of downstream transporter networks mediates nyctinastic leaf movement in peanut.
papers.summary: Combined temporal transcriptome profiling, photoperiod manipulation, and tissue-specific expression analysis in peanut to dissect molecular regulation of nyctinastic leaf movement. Identified rhythmic light- and circadian-related genes, including SWEET and aquaporin transporters and a pulvinus-enriched MYB transcription factor, supporting a model where photoreceptors and the circadian clock coordinate transporter and regulatory gene expression.

papers.title: Niosome-mediated melatonin delivery via SilMA/GelMA microneedles promotes healing of sleep deprivation-aggravated oral ulcers.
papers.summary: Develops a melatonin-loaded niosome-incorporated SilMA/GelMA composite hydrogel microneedle (Nio-MT@S-G MN) for localized delivery to oral ulcers aggravated by sleep deprivation. In vitro and in mice, the microneedle reduced neutrophil extracellular traps, restored epithelial barrier proteins, and significantly accelerated ulcer closure, identifying excessive NETs as a key mediator linking sleep deprivation to delayed oral wound healing.

papers.title: Global Research Trends in Sleep Quality, Sleep Deprivation and Sleep Promotion Among ICU Patients: A Descriptive and Evaluative Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.summary: A bibliometric analysis of 379 publications from 1983 to 2026 revealed a significant positive trend in ICU sleep research output and identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation', and 'delirium' as motor themes, with emerging concepts including circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain, and anxiety. The field's thematic structure guides targeted sleep promotion protocols in critical care.

papers.title: Beyond processed depth targets: frontal EEG patterns, brain vulnerability, and postoperative delirium in older adults.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
papers.summary: This narrative review examines whether frontal EEG signals beyond processed depth indices provide information about postoperative delirium risk in older adults, synthesizing evidence from randomized trials and observational studies. It concludes that processed EEG-guided titration alone does not reliably prevent delirium, but patterns such as reduced frontal alpha power and burst suppression offer contextual information about brain vulnerability, supporting a multimodal interpretation framework.

papers.title: Distinct brain activation patterns linked to clinical symptoms during hand grasping in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Investigated brain functional activation during a hand grasping task in 59 Parkinson's disease patients using functional near-infrared spectroscopy and examined associations with clinical symptoms. Found that constipation was positively correlated with activation in prefrontal-premotor regions during left-hand task, while freezing of gait was negatively correlated with hemodynamic persistence in the right primary motor cortex during right-hand task.

papers.title: Spaceflight human optimization and performance: positioning astronauts in an operational framework to promote health, fitness, and mission readiness.
papers.summary: Presents a theoretical framework for optimizing astronaut health and performance during spaceflight by integrating concepts from aerospace medicine, human performance, sports science, and nutrition. Proposes that mission readiness can be enhanced through individualized exercise countermeasures, health monitoring, precision nutrition, and behavioral readiness programs, with continuous monitoring enabling data-driven decisions across all mission phases.

papers.title: Associations between perceived stress, sleep quality, and suicidal ideation among Chinese graduating-grade secondary school students: a multi-method study of the moderating role of physical exercise.
papers.summary: Surveyed 4,372 Chinese graduating-grade secondary school students to examine associations among perceived stress, sleep quality, physical exercise, and suicidal ideation using mediation, moderation, machine-learning, and network analyses. Found that sleep quality partially mediated the association between perceived stress and suicidal ideation, and physical exercise moderated these relationships, with machine-learning models achieving R2 ~0.41 and network analysis identifying sleep quality, stress-coping burden, and exercise frequency as highly connected nodes.

papers.title: Vanillin alleviates circadian disruption-induced cognitive impairment: involvement of gut microbiota alterations and tryptophan metabolism.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of circadian disruption, oral vanillin improved spatial learning and recognition memory and corrected abnormal tryptophan, kynurenine, and kynurenic acid levels. Vanillin also modulated gut microbiota composition and diversity, enhanced intestinal barrier function and immune homeostasis, and reduced hippocampal astrocyte activation.

papers.title: Associations Between Dietary Habits and Sleep Duration in Japanese Children: The Fukushima Health Management Survey.
papers.journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
papers.summary: In 28,429 children aged 1–15 years from the Fukushima Health Management Survey, cross-sectional analyses found that each one-point increase in dietary habit scores was associated with slightly longer sleep duration (coefficients 0.018–0.024 hours per score unit), while longitudinal associations were not statistically significant after multivariable adjustment. Among adolescents aged 13–15 years, each one-point increase in the 11-item dietary score was associated with higher odds of adequate sleep time (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02–1.09).

papers.title: Feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary estimates of a multimodal AKTIVER Heart Delirium Prevention Program in patients indicated for cardiac surgery: study protocol of a randomized controlled PREVENT POstoperative Delirium (PREVENT-POD) Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized controlled pilot trial (PREVENT-POD) that will recruit 60 cardiac surgery patients aged 65 or older to assess the feasibility and acceptability of a multimodal non-pharmacological AKTIVER Heart delirium prevention program versus treatment-as-usual plus. Secondary outcomes include preliminary estimates of postoperative delirium incidence, duration, and severity, as well as cognition, quality of life, sleep, distress, depression, and anxiety.

papers.title: Reminder Strategies to Improve Meal-Logging Adherence: Protocol for a Microrandomized Trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a microrandomized trial embedded in a 4-week observational lifestyle phenotyping study (N=200) to test whether loss-framed or logging-consistency reminders improve adherence to image-based meal logging compared with a neutral reminder. The proximal outcome is meal logging within 2 hours of a reminder, analyzed using marginal excursion effect models; enrollment began in November 2025 and results are expected in Q2 2027.

papers.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Pain Chronification: Neuroimmune Rationale, Evidence Boundaries, and Trial Design Priorities: A Structured Narrative Review.
papers.summary: A structured narrative review evaluated cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) as an early, mechanism-informed intervention in pain chronification by synthesizing prespecified evidence domains on neuroimmune/glial mechanisms, brain-network mechanisms, CBT outcomes, and trial design. It found translational support for neuroimmune contributions to central sensitization but insufficient human evidence for direct CBT effects on microglial or astrocytic activation, while CBT showed reproducible small effects on pain intensity and more consistent benefits for interference, disability, distress, coping, sleep, and function, leading the authors to recommend risk-stratified, component-specific, mechanism-embedded trials.

papers.title: A serum cytokine-derived integrated inflammatory profile score (IIPS) links systemic inflammation to symptom burden and severity in COPD.
papers.summary: The study derived an Integrated Inflammatory Profile Score (IIPS) from serum cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-10) in 62 stable COPD patients, finding it significantly associated with FEV1% predicted (R2=0.1867) and better at discriminating spirometric severity (AUC=0.7381) than individual cytokines. IIPS showed only trend-level associations with symptom domains like sleep and energy, suggesting limited explanatory power for patient-reported burden.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
